rows.label: Step rate
rows.note: Twice the stride rate of the tracked leg (assumes left and right steps are alike).

rows.label: Flight time per step (estimated)
rows.note: Half the stride time minus contact time; assumes symmetry.

rows.label: Foot-strike angle
rows.note: Classified as rearfoot strike (rearfoot above 8 deg, forefoot below -1.6 deg; thresholds from 9 midfoot strikes in 20 runners). Foot-flat is taken from mid-stance here, not from standing as in the source.

rows.label: Shank angle at contact
rows.note: Positive = ankle ahead of the knee ("extended tibia"). The source describes vertical or flexed as preferable for impact-related injuries, without a cutoff.

ref.basis: Typical peak stance knee flexion approaches about 45 deg; under 40 deg has been associated with some patellofemoral pain subgroups. The source states that no injury cutoffs exist.
ref.citation: Souza (2016) Phys Med Rehabil Clin N Am 27(1):217-36

rows.label: Ankle ahead of the hip at contact
rows.note: Larger values indicate reaching (overstriding). The source uses a yes/no check of whether a vertical line from the ankle falls within the pelvis.

rows.label: Ankle ahead of the centre of mass at contact
rows.note: Centre of mass is a body-model estimate.

rows.label: Thigh behind vertical at toe-off
rows.note: A surrogate for hip extension in late stance. No target: the source says the optimal amount is unknown.

rows.label: Vertical movement of the centre of mass
Step length (from the speed you entered)

caveats: Keypoints are model estimates. Published 2D joint-angle errors for this type of model are about 5 deg or more, and the foot keypoints are among the least certain.
Foot contact and toe-off are detected from foot position relative to the pelvis, a method validated for walking (Zeni et al., 2008), not running. It is unvalidated on real runners in this tool.

The source framework states that no cutoffs for abnormal running kinematics exist, and that changing running form in uninjured runners is not evidence-based. Treat the options as things to explore, not corrections.
This tool cannot assess pain or injury.
